author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Create a reproducible PS2 emulation performance report
summary: Package device and software identity, game serial and hash, exact settings, normal save, timed route, cold and warm results, logs, screenshots, expected behavior, and one-variable comparisons into a report another tester can replay.
heroAlt: PCSX2 game summary showing serial, file path, CRC, region, and verified-disc identity for a reproducible report

blocks.text: Make the route replayable by someone else

A useful report describes a specific workload rather than saying a game is slow. Include the device, Android build, GPU driver when visible, emulator version, game serial and region, verified image hash, exact per-game profile, and a normal save. Define inputs and timestamps from boot to the slow scene, then attach both cold and warm results so cache behavior is not confused with sustained performance.
Do not upload copyrighted disc images, BIOS files, personal account data, or saves containing sensitive information. Share the smallest lawful evidence bundle needed to reproduce the problem.

items: Device model, SoC, Android build, driver, emulator version, and power mode.
Game title, serial, region, revision, and private hash record.
Export or screenshots of every relevant global and per-game setting.
A normal save before a deterministic route and written input sequence.
Logs and timing capture beginning before the title launches.

blocks.text: Build the report from baseline to controlled comparison

items: 1. Cold-boot the title and follow the written route without changing settings.
2. Mark the first bad frame, audio change, and frame-time interval with timestamps.
3. Replay immediately to produce a warm-cache result.
4. Run one justified single-variable comparison such as native resolution or alternate renderer.
5. Restore baseline and confirm the symptom returns.
6. Trim logs to the relevant session while keeping initialization and error context.
7. Attach screenshots of the scene, counters, and settings with readable labels.
8. Write expected behavior, actual behavior, frequency, safety notes, and exact reproduction steps.

blocks.text: Cold, warm, and restored-baseline passes answer whether the problem is cache-related and whether the controlled variable actually affects it. Hardware and content identity let another tester distinguish a platform regression from a regional game difference. A normal save avoids savestate version coupling.
A second tester should be able to reconstruct the route and know exactly what evidence would confirm or refute the report.

items: Device, system, emulator, and game identity are complete.
Settings are exact rather than described as default.
The route begins from a normal save with timed landmarks.
Cold, warm, comparison, and restored-baseline results are separated.
Logs and images contain no private or copyrighted payloads.
Several settings differ in the comparison: rerun one variable at a time.
The save depends on an incompatible savestate: create a normal save route.
Logs begin after the slowdown: capture initialization and lead-in.
The report says 'latest' instead of versions: replace with exact identifiers.

blocks.text: Return the test device to daily settings

Restore the accepted per-game profile, disable verbose logging and overlays, remove temporary test copies, and verify a normal save load. Keep the sanitized report bundle and original notes separate so future updates can repeat the same route.
A hash proves identity, not ownership
Record hashes privately or in the report when appropriate, but never attach the disc image or BIOS. Testers must reproduce with their own lawful dumps and matching regional content.
